Q: using sed to replace multiple lines between two patterns A:

This might work for you (GNU sed):

sed '/BEGIN/{:a;N;/END/!ba;s#.*#echo "&"|sed "3~2s/./X/g"#e}' file

Slurp up the lines between BEGIN and END and pass them to a second invocation of sed using the e flag of the substitution command.

Q: How can I use tailwindcss without internet? A:

You can use these commands:

npm install -g tailwindcss
npx tailwindcss init

content: ['./src/**/*.{html,js,vue,ts}'],

And after work offline

Q: Using subquery as a derived table A:

Let's first see the query:

SELECT SaleID, CarID, CustomerID, LocationID, SalesRepID, SaleAmount, SaleDate
FROM Sale
WHERE EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM Customer
    WHERE Customer.CustomerID = Sales.CustomerID AND
          Customer.Gender = 'F'
)

So let's see what happens above:

  • we have an inner query where we select from Customer
  • where the CustomerID of Customer matches its counterpart of Sales in the outer query as well as the Gender is being checked
  • we select 1 in the subquery because we don't care about the fields of the Customer in this query
  • in the outer query we select from Sale
  • on the condition that there EXISTS a female Customer whose CustomerID matches the one from Sales
  • we explicitly SELECT all fields from Sales because even though now we want all fields, later on the schema of the table may change with fields you do not want to select, like a future field representing a QR code

Why your query was incorrect: consider the example of duplicated CustomerID in the Customer table (nothing stated that it's a primary key, which intuitively should be the case, but we cannot presume that from the spec.), so if you have two Customer records whose CustomerID is the same and their Gender is F, then should you have a Sales record matching the given duplicated CustomerID, then the result will duplicate the Sales record misleading the person evaluating the results.
